source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The fully observed S-ID paper states necessary-and-sufficient graphical conditions and a sound-and-complete algorithm for S-ID.
Conditioning commutes with intervention only for non-ancestors of the conditioning variables and preserves selected-subpopulation causal semantics in that regime.

The paper proves a sound and complete c-gID algorithm under an explicit positivity assumption and uses novel positive completeness constructions; its setting is conditional generalized identification, not selected-law latent S-ID.

The article reduces discrete causal bounding problems to polynomial programming and computes sharp bounds, including under selection, but does not state a latent S-ID completeness or S-Hedge certificate theorem.
The paper studies full-population ATE identifiability under selection bias through probability-class assumptions; this is orthogonal to arbitrary-ADMG selected-subpopulation graphwise identification.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Repair def:s-hedge by requiring SComp(C)={C}, then restate the projection lemma and inverse-lift OEQ only for terminal Algorithm 1 calls with the corresponding C,D_i,T_i relation explicit.

Replace the unsupported global call-count formula by a proved bound based on the initial number of calls and the sum of their initial enclosing-component sizes, or prove disjointness/injectivity sufficient for the advertised |N_S|+|D_S(D)| bound.

Solve and record the exact symbolic selected-law fiber for G_star before attempting the universal lift; if it fails, promote the maximal incidence class and its inclusion relation to the headline theorem.

recommended_next_step: Revise the S-Hedge predicate and dependent statements to match the published terminal-failure geometry, audit the algorithmic call bound, then advance the repaired inverse-lift kernel to Stage 0.
